entries.title: Large expected overlap does not force intersection
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. Two independent connected paths with specified pairs of endpoints can have E I=N tending to infinity while P(I>0)=1/N tends to zero, where I counts their common vertices. In the explicit corridor construction E I=N, E I^2=N^3, P(I>0)=1/N; the graph can have maximum degree three.
assumptions: Independent uniform corridor labels J,K in {1,...,N}
L=N^2 common vertices in each disjoint corridor
Four distinct source endpoints; only equal labels cause intersection

entries.title: A fourth-moment deficit survives weak convergence
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. If centered real X_n have E X_n^2=1 and E X_n^4<=3-delta for fixed delta>0, every weak subsequential limit is centered, has variance one and fourth moment at most 3-delta, and is non-Gaussian. Fourth-moment equality under the limit is unnecessary; second-moment uniform integrability and a truncated fourth-moment bound suffice.

entries.title: The original-current weighted fourth-moment criterion
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For a finite free-boundary zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model and weights f_x>=0, let V=E(sum f_x sigma_x)^2>0. Under Q_f(x1,...,x4)=f1 f2 f3 f4 G12 G34/V^2, E X_f^4=3-2 E_Q p, where p is connection of x1 to x3 in the original union of two currents with parity source pairs 12 and 34. A uniform positive E_Q p gives a scalar fourth-moment deficit. Its 3D lower bound remains unproved.
assumptions: Finite graph, zero field, nonnegative couplings, free boundary
Define p arbitrarily, e.g. zero, on zero-Q tuples with unsupported sources

entries.title: A quadratic current comparison on finite trees
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For finite ferromagnetic trees at zero field and free boundary, original two-source-current connection q and meeting r of the independently sourceless-augmented source components satisfy q >= (e/4) r^2. The constant is asymptotically sharp among paths. This rules out treating failure of a linear comparison as failure of every quantitative transfer; the full cyclic Z^3 case remains unproved.
assumptions: Four independent currents with source pairs ab,cd,empty,empty

entries.title: C0052 source quantifiers and normalization
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. The original source definition asks g(beta) not to tend to zero; it is equivalent to a nonzero limsup of -g, not by definition to an infimum over every scale and unspecified source placement of a current intersection probability. For zero-field nearest-neighbor Ising on Z^3, g=sum U4(0,x2,x3,x4)/(chi^2 xi^3)<=0, with xi the exponential correlation length. The original goal is a sequence beta_n increasing to beta_c with -g(beta_n)>=epsilon>0; uniqueness or all-subsequence non-Gaussianity is not supplied by this definition.
assumptions: No theorem equating unspecified pointwise and integrated criteria is assumed

entries.title: Cycle parity blocks tree edge independence
entries.statement: DRAFT; independent mathematical review pending. For a sourceless random current on a uniform four-edge cycle at t>0, the odd-edge indicators are all the same Bernoulli variable of parameter h=tanh(t)^4/(1+tanh(t)^4). Hence E[B_e B_f]=h>h^2=E B_e E B_f for distinct edges; conditioning on the source set alone does not give independent edge values. The finite-tree comparison q>=e*r^2/4 therefore requires a new dependence argument before any extension to the full critical Z^3 lattice.
assumptions: Finite four-cycle, zero field, free boundary
One current with empty parity source set

relations.rationale: The weighted criterion yields E X^4=3-2 E_Q p; the weak-limit lemma turns a uniform deficit into non-Gaussianity.
The corridor example supplies E I=N but P(I>0)=1/N, showing why an expected-count lower bound alone cannot prove the required E_Q p floor.
The finite-tree q>=e*r^2/4 comparison addresses transferring an augmented meeting lower bound to original-current connection; no cyclic-lattice transfer is claimed.
Existing unverified card asserts equivalence to inf over scales L. This draft records the source nonzero-limsup criterion, exact normalization, and the missing endpoint/cutoff argument.

The nonlinear entry requires a finite tree, where sources fix each edge parity. The cycle entry exhibits a shared parity bit with E[B_e B_f]=h rather than h^2, documenting why that factorization cannot extend unchanged.
